row k and column k of the diagonal tile do not change while k\n// is being processed (dist[k][k] == 0), so this matches the sequential order.\ntemplate <size_t B>\nstatic inline void tileDependent(unsigned int* C, unsigned int* P,\n                                 const unsigned int* A, const unsigned int* Bm,\n                                 const unsigned int kBase) {\n    for (size_t k = 0; k < B; ++k) {\n        const unsigned int kv = kBase + static_cast<unsigned int>(k);\n        const unsigned int* rowK = Bm + k * B;\n        for (size_t i = 0; i < B; ++i) {\n            const unsigned int distIK = A[i * B + k];\n            unsigned int* rowI = C + i * B;\n            unsigned int* pathI = P + i * B;\n            #pragma omp simd\n            for (size_t j = 0; j < B; ++j) {\n                const unsigned int newDist = distIK + rowK[j];\n                const bool better = newDist < rowI[j];\n                rowI[j] = better ? newDist : rowI[j];\n                pathI[j] = better ? kv : pathI[j];\n            }\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n// Tile update where C is disjoint from A and B. Each chunk of a row of C is kept\n// in registers across the whole k loop (k is still processed in increasing order\n// for every element).\ntemplate <size_t B>\nstatic inline void tileIndependent(unsigned int* __restrict C, unsigned int* __restrict P,\n                                   const unsigned int* __restrict A,\n                                   const unsigned int* __restrict Bm,\n                                   const unsigned int kBase) {\n    constexpr size_t CHUNK = (B < 32) ? B : 32;\n    for (size_t i = 0; i < B; ++i) {\n        const unsigned int* rowA = A + i * B;\n        for (size_t jc = 0; jc < B; jc += CHUNK) {\n            unsigned int cd[CHUNK];\n            unsigned int cp[CHUNK];\n            #pragma omp simd\n            for (size_t j = 0; j < CHUNK; ++j) {\n                cd[j] = C[i * B + jc + j];\n                cp[j] = P[i * B + jc + j];\n            }\n            for (size_t k = 0; k < B; ++k) {\n                const unsigned int distIK = rowA[k];\n                const unsigned int kv = kBase + static_cast<unsigned int>(k);\n                const unsigned int* rowK = Bm + k * B + jc;\n                #pragma omp simd\n                for (size_t j = 0; j < CHUNK; ++j) {\n                    const unsigned int newDist = distIK + rowK[j];\n                    const bool better = newDist < cd[j];\n                    cd[j] = better ? newDist : cd[j];\n                    cp[j] = better ? kv : cp[j];\n                }\n            }\n            #pragma omp simd\n            for (size_t j = 0; j < CHUNK; ++j) {\n                C[i * B + jc + j] = cd[j];\n                P[i * B + jc + j] = cp[j];\n            }\n        }\n    }\n}\n\ntemplate <size_t B>\nstatic void floydWarshallBlocked(std::vector<unsigned int>& dist,\n                                 std::vector<unsigned int>& path,\n                                 const size_t n) {\n    const size_t nb = (n + B - 1) / B;\n    const size_t tileElems = B * B;\n    const size_t numTiles = nb * nb;\n    const size_t total = numTiles * tileElems;\n\n    // Uninitialized, cache-line aligned buffers; first touched in parallel below\n    unsigned int* td = static_cast<unsigned int*>(std::aligned_alloc(64, total * sizeof(unsigned int)));\n    unsigned int* tp = static_cast<unsigned int*>(std::aligned_alloc(64, total * sizeof(unsigned int)));\n    if (!td || !tp) {\n        fprintf(stderr, \"Allocation failed\\n\");\n        std::exit(1);\n    }\n    unsigned int* const d = dist.data();\n    unsigned int* const p = path.data();\n\n    // Never use more threads than there are independent tiles per round\n    const size_t maxUseful = std::max<size_t>(1, (nb - 1) * (nb - 1));\n    const int numThreads = static_cast<int>(\n        std::min<size_t>(static_cast<size_t>(omp_get_max_threads()), maxUseful));\n\n    #pragma omp parallel num_threads(numThreads)\n    {\n        // Pack into tiled layout (same static tile distribution as phase 3 -> NUMA locality)\n        #pragma omp for schedule(static)\n        for (size_t t = 0; t < numTiles; ++t) {\n            const size_t ib = t / nb, jb = t % nb;\n            unsigned int* C = td + t * tileElems;\n            unsigned int* P = tp + t * tileElems;\n            for (size_t r = 0; r < B; ++r) {\n                const size_t gi = ib * B + r;\n                for (size_t c = 0; c < B; ++c) {\n                    const size_t gj = jb * B + c;\n                    if (gi < n && gj < n) {\n                        C[r * B + c] = d[gi * n + gj];\n                        P[r * B + c] = p[gi * n + gj];\n                    } else {\n                        C[r * B + c] = (gi == gj) ? 0u : INF;\n                        P[r * B + c] = static_cast<unsigned int>(gi);\n                    }\n                }\n            }\n        }\n        // implicit barrier\n\n        for (size_t kb = 0; kb < nb; ++kb) {\n            const unsigned int kBase = static_cast<unsigned int>(kb * B);\n            unsigned int* const D = td + (kb * nb + kb) * tileElems;\n\n            // Phase 1: diagonal tile\n            #pragma omp single\n            tileDependent<B>(D, tp + (kb * nb + kb) * tileElems, D, D, kBase);\n            // implicit barrier\n\n            // Phase 2: tiles in tile-row kb and tile-column kb\n            #pragma omp for schedule(dynamic, 1)\n            for (size_t t = 0; t < 2 * nb; ++t) {\n                const size_t b = t >> 1;\n                if (b == kb) continue;\n                if (t & 1) {\n                    // column tile (b, kb): C[i][j] = min(C[i][j], C[i][k] + D[k][j])\n                    const size_t ti = b * nb + kb;\n                    unsigned int* C = td + ti * tileElems;\n                    tileDependent<B>(C, tp + ti * tileElems, C, D, kBase);\n                } else {\n                    // row tile (kb, b): C[i][j] = min(C[i][j], D[i][k] + C[k][j])\n                    const size_t ti = kb * nb + b;\n                    unsigned int* C = td + ti * tileElems;\n                    tileDependent<B>(C, tp + ti * tileElems, D, C, kBase);\n                }\n            }\n            // implicit barrier\n\n            // Phase 3: all remaining tiles are independent of each other\n            #pragma omp for schedule(static)\n            for (size_t t = 0; t < numTiles; ++t) {\n                const size_t ib = t / nb, jb = t % nb;\n                if (ib == kb || jb == kb) continue;\n                tileIndependent<B>(td + t * tileElems, tp + t * tileElems,\n                                   td + (ib * nb + kb) * tileElems,\n                                   td + (kb * nb + jb) * tileElems, kBase);\n            }\n            // implicit barrier\n        }\n\n        // Unpack back to the row-major layout\n        #pragma omp for schedule(static)\n        for (size_t gi = 0; gi < n; ++gi) {\n            const size_t ib = gi / B, r = gi % B;\n            for (size_t jb = 0; jb < nb; ++jb) {\n                const size_t off = (ib * nb + jb) * tileElems + r * B;\n                const size_t cEnd = std::min(B, n - jb * B);\n                for (size_t c = 0; c < cEnd; ++c) {\n                    d[gi * n + jb * B + c] = td[off + c];\n                    p[gi * n + jb * B + c] = tp[off + c];\n                }\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    std::free(td);\n    std::free(tp);\n}\n\nvoid floydWarshall(std::vector<unsigned int>& dist, \n                   std::vector<unsigned int>& path, \n                   const size_t numNodes) {\n    if (numNodes == 0) return;\n    // Smaller tiles expose more parallelism for small graphs\n    if (numNodes <= 1024) {\n        floydWarshallBlocked<32>(dist, path, numNodes);\n    } else {\n        floydWarshallBlocked<64>(dist, path, numNodes);\n    }\n}\n\n'''\ns=s[:start]+new+s[end:]\nopen(p,'w').write(s)\nEOF\ncmake --build /tmp/fwb 2>&1 | grep -E \"warn|error\"; newDist : rowI[j];\n                pathI[j] = better ? kv : pathI[j];\n            }\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n// Tile update where C is disjoint from A and B. Each chunk of a row of C is kept\n// in registers across the whole k loop (k is still processed in increasing order\n// for every element).\ntemplate <size_t B>\nstatic inline void tileIndependent(unsigned int* __restrict C, unsigned int* __restrict P,\n                                   const unsigned int* __restrict A,\n                                   const unsigned int* __restrict Bm,\n                                   const unsigned int kBase) {\n    constexpr size_t CHUNK = (B < 32) ? j < CHUNK; ++j) {\n                    const unsigned int newDist = distIK + rowK[j];\n                    const bool better = newDist < cd[j];\n                    cd[j] = better ? newDist : cd[j];\n                    cp[j] = better ? kv : cp[j];\n                }\n            }\n            #pragma omp simd\n            for (size_t j = 0; j < CHUNK; ++j) {\n                C[i * B + jc + j] = cd[j];\n                P[i * B + jc + j] = cp[j];\n            }\n        }\n    }\n}\n\ntemplate <size_t B>\nstatic void floydWarshallBlocked(std::vector<unsigned int>& dist,\n                                 std::vector<unsigned int>& path,\n                                 const size_t n) {\n    const size_t nb = (n + B - 1) / B;\n    const size_t tileElems = B * B;\n    const size_t numTiles = nb * nb;\n    const size_t total = numTiles * tileElems;\n\n    // Uninitialized, cache-line aligned buffers; first touched in parallel below\n    unsigned int* td = static_cast<unsigned int*>(std::aligned_alloc(64, total * sizeof(unsigned int)));\n    unsigned int* tp = static_cast<unsigned int*>(std::aligned_alloc(64, total * sizeof(unsigned int)));\n    if (!td || !tp) {\n        fprintf(stderr, \"Allocation failed\\n\");\n        std::exit(1);\n    }\n    unsigned int* const d = dist.data();\n    unsigned int* const p = path.data();\n\n    // Never use more threads than there are independent tiles per round\n    const size_t maxUseful = std::max<size_t>(1, (nb - 1) * (nb - 1));\n    const int numThreads = static_cast<int>(\n        std::min<size_t>(static_cast<size_t>(omp_get_max_threads()), maxUseful));\n\n    #pragma omp parallel num_threads(numThreads)\n    {\n        // Pack into tiled layout (same static tile distribution as phase 3 -> NUMA locality)\n        #pragma omp for schedule(static)\n        for (size_t t = 0; t < numTiles; ++t) {\n            const size_t ib = t / nb, jb = t % nb;\n            unsigned int* C = td + t * tileElems;\n            unsigned int* P = tp + t * tileElems;\n            for (size_t r = 0; r < B; ++r) {\n                const size_t gi = ib * B + r;\n                for (size_t c = 0; c < B; ++c) {\n                    const size_t gj = jb * B + c;\n                    if (gi < n && gj < n) {\n                        C[r * B + c] = d[gi * n + gj];\n                        P[r * B + c] = p[gi * n + gj];\n                    } else {\n                        C[r * B + c] = (gi == gj) ? 0u : INF;\n                        P[r * B + c] = static_cast<unsigned int>(gi);\n                    }\n                }\n            }\n        }\n        // implicit barrier\n\n        for (size_t kb = 0; kb < nb; ++kb) {\n            const unsigned int kBase = static_cast<unsigned int>(kb * B);\n            unsigned int* const D = td + (kb * nb + kb) * tileElems;\n\n            // Phase 1: diagonal tile\n            #pragma omp single\n            tileDependent<B>(D, tp + (kb * nb + kb) * tileElems, D, D, kBase);\n            // implicit barrier\n\n            // Phase 2: tiles in tile-row kb and tile-column kb\n            #pragma omp for schedule(dynamic, 1)\n            for (size_t t = 0; t < numTiles; ++t) {\n                const size_t ib = t / nb, jb = t % nb;\n                if (ib == kb || jb == kb) continue;\n                tileIndependent<B>(td + t * tileElems, tp + t * tileElems,\n                                   td + (ib * nb + kb) * tileElems,\n                                   td + (kb * nb + jb) * tileElems, kBase);\n            }\n            // implicit barrier\n        }\n\n        // Unpack back to the row-major layout\n        #pragma omp for schedule(static)\n        for (size_t gi = 0; gi < n; ++gi) {\n            const size_t ib = gi / B, r = gi % B;\n            for (size_t jb = 0; jb < nb; ++jb) {\n                const size_t off = (ib * nb + jb) * tileElems + r * B;\n                const size_t cEnd = std::min(B, n - jb * B);\n                for (size_t c = 0; c < cEnd; ++c) {\n                    d[gi * n + jb * B + c] = td[off + c];\n                    p[gi * n + jb * B + c] = tp[off + c];\n                }\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    std::free(td);\n    std::free(tp);\n}\n\nvoid floydWarshall(std::vector<unsigned int>& dist, \n                   std::vector<unsigned int>& path, \n                   const size_t numNodes) {\n    if (numNodes == 0) return;\n    // Smaller tiles expose more parallelism for small graphs\n    if (numNodes <= 1024) {\n        floydWarshallBlocked<32>(dist, path, numNodes);\n    } else {\n        floydWarshallBlocked<64>(dist, path, numNodes);\n    }\n}\n\n'''\ns=s[:start]+new+s[end:]\nopen(p,'w').write(s)\nEOF\ncmake --build /tmp/fwb 2>&1 | grep -E \"warn|error\"; {"type":"assistant","message":{"model":"claude-opus-5-5","id":"msg_011Cff4vJjSkf5jRaC6q48B5","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"text","text":"I parallelized the benchmark with OpenMP. The distance matrix (the result the program checks and prints) matches the original exactly. The path matrix doesn't always match: when there are ties, it can record a different intermediate node. It's never printed or validated, so nothing visible changes, but the semantics aren't strictly identical (details at the end).\n\n**Results on this machine (2× EPYC 7763, 256 hardware threads), default settings, no environment variables:**\n\n| n | Original | Parallel | Speedup |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| 512 (default) | 165 ms | ~4–6 ms | ~30× |\n| 2048 | 9395 ms | ~29 ms | ~320× |\n| 4096 | — | ~115 ms | — |\n| 8192 | — | ~660 ms | — |\n\nAt n=4096, going from 1 to 32 threads scales almost linearly (6370 → 256 ms). Beyond that it levels off (64 → 162 ms, 128 → 119 ms, 256 → 118 ms) because it hits memory bandwidth. Part of the overall gain comes from a faster single-thread kernel (about 12× faster than the original even on one thread).\n\n**Correctness:** the distance hash matches the original exactly for n = 0, 2, 31, 33, 63, 65, 129, 777, 1025, 1500, 2048 and 3000, with 1, 3 and 256 threads. `-v` validation passes for all of these and for n = 512, 1000 and 4096. It builds without warnings, and the executable is still called `floydwarshall`.\n\n**What changed in `floydwarshall.cpp`:**\n- **Tiled algorithm:** the standard three-phase blocked Floyd-Warshall. For each block of intermediate nodes it updates the diagonal tile, then the tiles in its row and column, then all remaining tiles in parallel. Tiles are 64×64, or 32×32 when n ≤ 1024 to give small graphs more parallel work.\n- **Repacked memory layout:** for the computation, the matrices are copied into a layout where each tile is contiguous, padded to a whole number of tiles with \"infinite\" distances, then copied back. With power-of-two sizes, the original row layout made the 64 rows of a tile collide in the same cache sets, which made tile updates about 4× slower. The padding can't shorten any real path. The copies run in parallel, so each thread's tiles stay in its own memory.\n- **Faster inner loops:** the update loops are branch-free and vectorized. For the tiles updated in the last phase, a chunk of each row stays in registers across all the intermediate nodes.\n- **Spin barrier between phases:** the OpenMP default made idle threads go to sleep between the short phases, and timings varied from 30 ms to 400 ms at n=2048. A small spinning barrier makes them stable. It yields when there are more threads than cores, so 512 threads still give the right answer (318 ms).\n- **Thread pinning:** without it, run times varied widely. If you haven't set `OMP_PLACES`, each thread pins itself to a CPU during the untimed setup. If you have set `OMP_PLACES` or `OMP_PROC_BIND`, those are used instead.\n- **Thread count:** the program never starts more threads than there are independent tiles, which helps small graphs.\n- The random matrix setup stays serial so the generated graph is identical. The path matrix setup now runs in parallel and produces the same values.\n\n`CMakeLists.txt` now does `find_package(OpenMP REQUIRED)` and links `OpenMP::OpenMP_CXX`. Nothing else was added.\n\n**About the path matrix:** each entry is still a valid intermediate node on a shortest path, and all distances are identical. But on ties, the tiled algorithm may record a different node than the original, because it updates entries in a different order. A temporary build that also hashed the path matrix confirmed the hashes differ. If you need the path matrix to match exactly, the alternative is the simple version that parallelizes each intermediate-node step separately. That keeps it bit-identical but synchronizes n times and needs much more memory bandwidth, so it would be a lot slower."}],"container":null,"stop_reason":null,"stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":759,"cache_read_input_tokens":52777,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":759},"output_tokens":5,"service_tier":"standard","inference_geo":"not_available"},"input_transformations":[],"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"6caf1f1e-15b6-4c6f-8353-c6bb9e7ab7e7","uuid":"382ae9b5-6129-4290-9892-1df25b726090","timestamp":"2026-10-03T09:29:39.531Z","request_id":"req_011Cff4vJGAuJ9qF1BNmWkgG"}
